450°F The cut depends on the food, so one number is never the whole answer. Each cell gives the air fryer temperature, °C, gas mark and the share of the oven time you save. Food Basket Oven-style General / mixed 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 12% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 15% less time Fries & potatoes 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 22% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 25% less time Chicken wings 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 12% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 15% less time Chicken breast (boneless) 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 17% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 20% less time Chicken thighs / bone-in 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 12% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 15% less time Steak & thick cuts 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 12% less time Capped 435°F / 225°C Gas mark 7 · 15% less time Fish & salmon 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 12% less time Capped 435°F / 225°C Gas mark 7 · 15% less time Bacon 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 22% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 25% less time Vegetables 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 17% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 20% less time Baked goods & cookies 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 7% less time Capped 435°F / 225°C Gas mark 7 · 10% less time Pizza & reheating 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 17% less time Capped 430°F / 220°C Gas mark 7 · 20% less time Casseroles & thick bakes 400°F / 205°C Gas mark 6 · 7% less time Capped 435°F / 225°C Gas mark 7 · 10% less time Capped: the converted temperature is above what the unit can reach (400°F basket, 450°F oven-style), so it is held at the maximum and part of the time cut is given back. What recipes use 450°F 450°F (230°C, gas mark 8) is the top end of home cooking: pizza on a stone, flatbreads, blistered tomatoes and peppers, smashed potatoes, hasselback potatoes, quick-roasted asparagus, and steak or chops seared at the end of a reverse sear. Recipes ask for it when the outside has to colour before the inside overcooks. A flat rule subtracts 25°F and stops there, but the result is not a setting a basket air fryer has. Every food in the table is capped at the basket maximum of 400°F, so the basket column shows the same temperature on every row and only the time varies. That is the honest answer: a basket air fryer cannot do 450°F, and the time has to make up the difference. The failure mode at 450°F: burnt top, wrong time Two things go wrong. The first is time. A chart that prints a basket temperature it cannot reach also cuts the time as if that heat existed, so the food comes out pale and underdone. Because the temperature is held at 400°F here, this converter gives back part of the cut: a general recipe saves about 12% of the oven time rather than the usual amount. The second is the surface. At the maximum the element runs flat out a few centimetres from the food, so tall items scorch on top, cheese and breadcrumbs burn before the base is crisp, and paper that is not pinned down can touch the element. Keep pizza and flatbreads thin, add cheese for the final few minutes if it browns early, and trim liners to the base of the basket. Worked example A pizza recipe says 450°F for 14 minutes. A basket air fryer is held at 400°F (205°C), so it takes 12 minutes; check the base at 8 minutes. An oven-style air fryer can run 430°F, below its own ceiling, and finishes in 11 minutes. The basket is the slower of the two here because it is the cooler one, the reverse of what happens at lower temperatures. 450°F in an oven-style air fryer Oven-style air fryers usually reach 450°F, so 450°F converts normally there: 430°F (220°C) with about 15% less time for a general recipe. If you own both kinds, or are choosing between them, this is the temperature where the difference shows. For pizza, flatbreads and anything you want charred, the oven-style unit is the better tool. A basket unit still makes good pizza and potatoes; it just needs the extra minutes the converter adds. In °C the recipe reads 230°C, and the basket setting is 205°C. Nearby temperatures 425°F oven to air fryer → Oven to air fryer converter (any temperature) → Printable conversion chart → Frozen food mode (packaging instructions) → Frequently asked questions What is 450°F in an air fryer? In a basket air fryer, 400°F (205°C) — its maximum — with about 12% less time. In an oven-style air fryer, 430°F with about 15% less time. Every food is capped in a basket unit. What is 450°F in Celsius for an air fryer? 450°F is 230°C, or gas mark 8. A basket air fryer tops out at 205°C, so set that and use the converted time. Why not subtract 25°F and set the result? Because a basket air fryer cannot reach it. The dial stops at 400°F, so the food cooks cooler than the chart assumed while the time was cut in full. Set 400°F and use the longer time the converter gives. Can I make pizza in the air fryer from a 450°F recipe? Yes. Use a pizza that fits flat, set 400°F in a basket unit and, for a 14-minute recipe, check the base at 8 minutes. Add the cheese part-way if the top browns before the crust is crisp. Is it safe to run an air fryer at its maximum temperature? Yes, it is designed for it. Keep it on a heat-proof surface with space behind the vent, never cover the basket completely with foil or paper, and empty the fat from the drawer so it does not smoke.
